name: Cloud Security — AWS, Azure & GCP
tagline: Posture audits, scoped offense, and public-bucket checks across AWS, Azure, and GCP — nested by provider and by function for your own accounts and sanctioned assessments.

tools.name: Prowler
tools.desc: Runs 1,000+ read-only checks across AWS, Azure, and GCP against CIS Benchmarks and 70+ compliance frameworks, with remediation guidance per finding.
tools.when: Kick off every posture review with it — the default for CIS/NIST alignment on any provider, driven via CLI, Docker, or the API.

tools.name: Scout Suite
tools.desc: NCC Group's multi-cloud auditor pulls configuration from provider APIs and renders a browsable point-in-time HTML report of risk areas for AWS, Azure, and GCP.
tools.when: Grab a clean visual report of config risk as a second opinion alongside Prowler; expect a quiet repo — last major release was 2022.

tools.name: CloudSploit (Trivy Cloud)
tools.desc: Aqua's Node.js CSPM scanner covering AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI, and GitHub with CIS/PCI/HIPAA modes; actively developed as the open-source half of the hosted Aqua Trivy Cloud / Wave platform.
tools.when: Broad self-hosted multi-cloud config checks in CI; know that the maintained commercial route is Aqua Trivy Cloud.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/aquasecurity/cloudsploit.git && cd cloudsploit && npm install

tools.name: Steampipe
tools.desc: Run SQL queries over live AWS, Azure, GCP, and 200+ other APIs, then reuse the same queries for compliance benchmarks (CIS) and ad-hoc posture checks.
tools.when: When you want scriptable, queryable posture evidence: SQL across your accounts beats shell-script loops and feeds reporting directly.

tools.name: Pacu
tools.desc: The AWS exploitation framework: modular post-compromise attacks covering IAM privilege escalation, Lambda backdoors, log tampering, and EC2 RCE, with a session database for clean reporting.
tools.when: After you hold valid-but-least-privilege AWS keys and want to demonstrate what an attacker could escalate to — lab/own-account use only.

tools.name: CloudFox
tools.desc: Bishop Fox's situational-awareness enumerator maps exploitable attack paths across AWS (34 commands) plus early Azure/GCP coverage, writing loot files for other tools.
tools.when: Run `cloudfox aws --profile X all-checks` first on any fresh scope to learn the estate and spot privesc paths before deeper exploitation with Pacu.

tools.name: cloudpwn
tools.desc: Cloud & container penetration suite — AWS/GCP/Azure enumeration, S3, docker leaks, k8s secrets, terraform audit, vault, CSPM.
tools.when: Posture-testing your own cloud tenants and IaC repos.

tools.name: crownjewel
tools.desc: Cross-cloud identity federation auditor — Golden/Silver SAML, OAuth client-ID spoofing, OIDC validation, cross-cloud token replay; offline fixtures.
tools.when: Auditing federated identity trust boundaries across your clouds.

tools.name: Prowler (AWS)
tools.desc: Prowler pinned to AWS (`-p aws`): 300+ AWS-specific checks across CIS 1.x/2.x, NIST 800-53, and Well-Architected focus areas, with per-finding remediation and CSV/JSON/SARIF output.
tools.when: The primary AWS compliance gate in CI or on a schedule; run alongside GuardDuty-focused triage for config findings.

tools.name: Scout Suite (AWS)
tools.desc: Scout Suite run with AWS credentials: point-in-time dumps of IAM, S3, EC2, and Security Group posture into a navigable HTML report annotated with risk rules.
tools.when: Fast visual sweep of one AWS account when you want a self-contained report artifact to share, not another CLI table.
tools.install: pip3 install scoutsuite && scout aws --profile prod

tools.name: cloud-inquisitor
tools.desc: Riot Games' config-audit and incident-response platform: scans accounts against custom rules, auto-remediates (e.g., open S3 buckets), and ships a web dashboard; only lightly maintained since 2021.
tools.when: When you want rule-driven auto-remediation on legacy AWS estates and accept a quiet project — otherwise prefer Prowler or Steampipe.

tools.name: AWS CLI & Batch Scripts
tools.desc: The built-in `aws` CLI plus shell one-liners and jq pipelines for service inventory, bucket ACL listing, unused IAM keys, and cross-account drift — endless and dependency-free.
tools.when: Quick targeted checks while Prowler/Steampipe are overkill: `aws iam list-access-keys --no-user-paginate`, `aws s3api get-bucket-acl`, etc.

tools.name: PMapper
tools.desc: NCC Group's Principal Mapper builds a graph of IAM users/groups/roles and their effective permissions, then computes shortest privilege-escalation and takeover paths.
tools.when: Model least-privilege drift: generate the graph in minutes and query for principals reaching admin via any path.

tools.name: enumerate-iam
tools.desc: Brute-forces every read-only AWS API call against a credential set to print exactly which IAM permissions it holds.
tools.when: You recovered AWS keys of unknown privilege and need the permission list fast, before choosing an escalation path.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/andresriancho/enumerate-iam.git && cd enumerate-iam && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: IAMActionHunter
tools.desc: Collects and queries AWS IAM policy statements to surface users and roles holding privesc-relevant permissions (iam:create*, iam:put*...) and exports CSV; also ships as a Pacu module.
tools.when: Hunt least-privilege violations and privilege-escalation levers across a large account in minutes, then review the CSV.

tools.name: S3Scanner
tools.desc: Scans lists of bucket names across AWS and S3-compatible stores (GCP, DigitalOcean, Linode, Scaleway) for existence, tests every permission path for misconfigurations, and can enumerate or dump objects.
tools.when: Find your own exposed buckets at scale: feed candidate names, get back which are public, listable, or readable.

tools.name: Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark (docs)
tools.desc: Microsoft's authoritative Azure security baseline: control families (identity, network, storage, data protection) with CSPM tooling guidance and mapping to NIST/CIS regulatory frameworks.
tools.when: Your reference before running scanners — know which controls the tool checks and which ones Azure Policy/Defender must enforce, since no scanner covers a benchmark alone.
tools.install: Reference guide — no install; mapped controls ship as built-in Azure Policy initiatives

tools.name: Azure Threat Research Matrix (ATRM)
tools.desc: MSTIC's community threat matrix documenting Azure/AWS/GCP attack vectors (reconnaissance, persistence, privilege escalation) with real examples and KQL hunting queries.
tools.when: Understand how attackers actually move in a tenant so your posture checks and MicroBurst-style simulations target the realistic paths.

tools.name: Prowler (Azure)
tools.desc: Prowler pinned to Azure (`-p azure --az-cli-auth`): 100+ read-only checks over Entra ID, subscriptions, storage, key vault, and network config against CIS Microsoft Azure 1.x/2.x.
tools.when: The main automated Azure compliance pass in CI or on a schedule; complements but does not replace Azure Policy assignments.

tools.name: Scout Suite (Azure)
tools.desc: Scout Suite's Azure provider: one-command dump of subscription posture (ARM resources, RBAC, storage, NSGs) into an HTML report with risk annotations.
tools.when: A point-in-time visual Azure report that mirrors your AWS workflow and is easy to archive as an evidence artifact.

tools.name: MicroBurst
tools.desc: NetSPI's PowerShell toolkit for attacking Azure: service discovery, weak-config auditing, credential dumping (AzPasswords), and post-exploitation on VMs, Key Vault, and Automation accounts.
tools.when: The default Azure toolkit in authenticated engagements on your own tenant; Windows-only, so run it from a PowerShell host with the Az modules installed.

tools.name: Stormspotter
tools.desc: Microsoft Azure Red Team's attack-graph tool: collects subscription and ARM resources into Neo4j and renders the attack surface with pivot opportunities.
tools.when: Map a large tenant visually and find cross-resource pivot paths once you hold reader-level access in a sanctioned assessment.

tools.name: ATEAM
tools.desc: NetSPI's unauthenticated reconnaissance tool probes name permutations across App Services, Key Vault, Storage, DevOps, SharePoint, and Databricks to discover Azure resources and attribute tenant IDs.
tools.when: From outside, discover forgotten Azure resources whose names leak a tenant — ideal for attack-surface checks on your own domains before logging in.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/NetSPI/ATEAM.git && cd ATEAM && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: Scout Suite (GCP)
tools.desc: Scout Suite's GCP provider: gathers project posture across IAM, GCE, GCS, GKE, and Cloud SQL into a browsable HTML risk report, including Org-level IAM.
tools.when: The quickest visual read of GCP config risk in one project — pair with Prowler for covered CIS controls.
tools.install: pip3 install scoutsuite && scout gcloud --project-id PROJECT

tools.name: Prowler (GCP)
tools.desc: Prowler pinned to GCP (`-p gcp`): 100+ read-only checks against the Google Cloud CIS 1.x benchmark covering IAM, logging, networking, and storage.
tools.when: The compliance-first GCP pass in CI; best paired with its AWS/Azure siblings for org-wide reporting.

tools.name: Forseti (retired)
tools.desc: Google's old inventory-and-policy engine for detecting GCP misconfigurations; officially retired by the Google Cloud team and no longer developed.
tools.when: Only revisit for legacy estates already running it — for new work use Prowler/Scout Suite plus Policy Controller and Assured workloads.

tools.name: gcloud CLI & Scripted Audits
tools.desc: The `gcloud` CLI plus `gcloud asset`, IAM recommender, and `gcloud projects get-iam-policy` pipelines for fast targeted checks and drift reporting.
tools.when: Quick focused questions — who can do what in a project, which buckets changed, logging disabled — without a full scanner run.

tools.name: gcp-scanner
tools.desc: Google's scanner determines what a compromised credential can reach across GCE, GCS, GKE, Cloud SQL, BigQuery, KMS, and more, pulling from VM metadata, SA keys, or OAuth tokens.
tools.when: Assess blast radius after a leaked service account key or compromised VM, without needing gcloud installed.

tools.name: gcpwn
tools.desc: NetSPI's GCP and Workspace pentesting framework: enumerates and downloads project data, builds BloodHound OpenGraph models, and bundles credential and exploit tooling.
tools.when: Deep GCP/Workspace engagements where you want structured enumeration feeding BloodHound-style attack-path analysis.

tools.name: GCP IAM Privilege Escalation Toolkit
tools.desc: Rhino's documented GCP IAM privesc methods plus a scanner (enumerate_member_permissions.py then check_for_privesc.py) that flags principals able to escalate.
tools.when: Audit who in your projects could privilege-escalate to org ownership and validate hardened role design.

tools.name: GCPBucketBrute
tools.desc: Enumerates Google Storage buckets from keyword permutations and reports per-bucket access, flagging public, writable, and privilege-escalation-prone (storage.buckets.setIamPolicy) buckets.
tools.when: Check which of your GCS buckets are reachable or writable without auth, including escalations visible from a service account.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/RhinoSecurityLabs/GCPBucketBrute.git && cd GCPBucketBrute && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: Checkov
tools.desc: Prisma Cloud-maintained IaC static analyzer with 1,000+ built-in policies for Terraform (incl. plan output), CloudFormation, Kubernetes, Helm, Dockerfile, Bicep, ARM, and Serverless; graph-based and multi-resource aware.
tools.when: The default IaC gate: scan Terraform/K8s/Dockerfile in CI and on terraform plan to catch exposed resources and weak IAM before apply.

tools.name: tfsec
tools.desc: Fast Terraform-specific static scanner with 400+ rules and custom Rego/policy support; development has wound down as scanning moved into Trivy (trivy config).
tools.when: Lightweight, human-friendly Terraform warnings in pre-commit; for maintained updates run the same checks via Trivy config.

tools.name: Terrascan (archived)
tools.desc: Tenable's Rego-policy IaC scanner for Terraform, CloudFormation, ARM, K8s, Helm, and Docker; the repository was archived November 2025 and is read-only.
tools.when: Only for aligning with existing Terrascan policy sets on frozen pipelines — new IaC work should use Checkov or KICS.

tools.name: cfn-guard
tools.desc: AWS's official CloudFormation policy-as-code tool: validates templates and yes, live stacks, against declarative rules written in a purpose-built Guard DSL; ships AWS managed rule collections.
tools.when: Enforce organizational CloudFormation rules (allowlists, encryption, tag policies) in CI against templates before deploy.

tools.name: cfn-nag
tools.desc: Stelligent's rule-based CloudFormation linter that flags over-permissive IAM wildcards, plaintext secrets, and open security groups across templates.
tools.when: Fast, opinionated CloudFormation warnings with zero configuration; a solid first pass before cfn-guard rules.

tools.name: kube-bench
tools.desc: Aqua's CIS Kubernetes benchmark runner that checks control-plane nodes (kube-apiserver, etcd) and workloads against the CIS K8s Benchmark 1.9+ sections.
tools.when: Baseline your clusters against CIS on install and after upgrades; run from the node or via the official image.

tools.name: kube-score
tools.desc: Opinionated static analysis of Kubernetes object manifests scoring against best practices: resource requests, probes, securityContext, network policies.
tools.when: Per-manifest linting in CI for the small, common mistakes — complements policy-heavy gatekeepers like Kyverno and kube-bench.

tools.name: KICS
tools.desc: Checkmarx's open-source IaC scanner (Keeping Infrastructure as Code Secure) running thousands of queries across 20+ platforms — Terraform, K8s, Docker, Helm, CloudFormation, Ansible — with SARIF output and OPA/Rego custom queries.
tools.when: A complementary cross-check on IaC after Checkov, or the pick when you want OPA/Rego policy authoring (the slot archived Terrascan used to fill).

tools.name: Trivy
tools.desc: Aqua's all-in-one scanner: OS/library package CVEs in images and filesystems, SBOM generation, IaC misconfigs (absorbed tfsec), Kubernetes scanning, and registry CI — one binary, zero daemon.
tools.when: The single tool to add to a container build: `trivy image`, `trivy fs --scanners vuln,secret,misconfig`, and `trivy sbom` cover images to source in one install.
